interstitialad.on_click: Fired when the user taps the ad. No data.
interstitialad.on_close: Fired when the user closes the ad. No data.
interstitialad.on_error: Fired when the ad fails to load or to show; `event.data` is the error from Google Mobile Ads as text.
interstitialad.on_impression: Fired when the ad counts as seen. No data.
interstitialad.on_load: Fired when the ad has loaded and `show` can display it. No data.
interstitialad.on_open: Fired when the ad covers the screen. No data.
interstitialad.request: Targeting of the ad request: `{ keywords:, content_url:, non_personalized_ads:, neighboring_content_urls:, http_timeout:, extras: }`.
interstitialad.unit_id: Your AdMob interstitial ad unit id. Unset, the client loads Google's test interstitial unit.

line.paint: How the line is drawn, built with `paint(...)`: `color` (default black), `style` (`"fill"`, the default, or `"stroke"`), `stroke_width`, `stroke_cap` (`"butt"`, `"round"`, `"square"`), `stroke_join` (`"miter"`, `"round"`, `"bevel"`), `stroke_dash_pattern` (dash and gap lengths, for example `[8, 4]`), `blend_mode`, `anti_alias` (default true), `blur_image` and `gradient`. A line is always stroked, whatever `style` says.
line.x1: Horizontal position of the start point. Required.
line.x2: Horizontal position of the end point. Required.
line.y1: Vertical position of the start point. Required.
line.y2: Vertical position of the end point. Required.

linechart.animation: How the chart animates when its data changes: a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration:, curve: }` (default 150 ms, `"linear"`).
linechart.baseline_x: x value the top and bottom axis labels are counted from (default 0).
linechart.baseline_y: y value the left and right axis labels are counted from (default 0).
linechart.border: Border drawn around the plot area, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`. No border is drawn when unset.
linechart.bottom_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
linechart.height: Height in logical pixels. In a parent with unbounded height, such as a `column` in a scrolling page, the chart is at most 300 pixels tall; set `height` to change it.
linechart.horizontal_grid_lines: Horizontal grid lines as a hash: `interval` (in y units), `color`, `width` (default 2), `dash_pattern` (for example `[4, 4]`) and `gradient`. Pass `{}` for the default lines. No grid is drawn when both grid properties are unset.
linechart.interactive: When true (the default), touching the chart highlights the nearest point and shows its bubble. With `false` the chart ignores touches and draws the bubbles of the parts you mark `selected: true` instead.
linechart.left_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
linechart.max_x: Largest value on the x axis. Unset, the chart fits the points.
linechart.max_y: Largest value on the y axis. Unset, the chart fits the points.
linechart.min_x: Smallest value on the x axis. Unset, the chart fits the points.
linechart.min_y: Smallest value on the y axis. Unset, the chart fits the points.
linechart.on_event: Fired as the user touches or hovers the chart. `event.data` has `type` and `spots`, a list of `{ "bar_index" => line, "spot_index" => point }` hashes for the touched points (empty when none). `event.data["type"]` is the touch phase: `"tapDown"`, `"tapUp"`, `"tapCancel"`, `"panStart"`, `"panUpdate"`, `"panEnd"`, `"longPressStart"`, `"longPressMoveUpdate"`, `"longPressEnd"`, or on desktop and web `"pointerEnter"`, `"pointerHover"` and `"pointerExit"`. The chart sends an event only when this data changes.
linechart.point_line_end: y value where the vertical indicator line under a touched point ends. Unset, it ends at the point.
linechart.point_line_start: y value where the vertical indicator line under a touched point starts. Unset, it starts at the bottom of the chart.
linechart.right_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
linechart.tooltip: Style of the bubble shown when a point is touched, as a hash: `bgcolor`, `border_radius`, `margin`, `padding`, `max_width`, `rotation`, `horizontal_offset`, `horizontal_alignment` (`"left"`, `"center"` or `"right"`), `border_side`, `fit_inside_horizontally` and `fit_inside_vertically`. Ruflet cannot set the text of a bubble yet, so a chart with `tooltip` set shows no bubble at all; leave it unset to get the default bubble with the touched value. Line charts also take `show_on_top_of_chart_box_area`.
linechart.top_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
linechart.vertical_grid_lines: Vertical grid lines as a hash: `interval` (in x units), `color`, `width` (default 2), `dash_pattern` and `gradient`. Pass `{}` for the default lines.

linechartdata.above_line: Vertical lines from each point to the top of the chart, as `{ color:, width:, dash_pattern: }`; needs an above-line fill too.
linechartdata.above_line_bgcolor: Fills the area between the line and the top of the chart with this color.
linechartdata.above_line_cutoff_y: Stops the area above the line at this y value.
linechartdata.above_line_gradient: Fills the area above the line with a gradient instead.
linechartdata.below_line: Vertical lines from each point down to the bottom of the chart, as `{ color:, width:, dash_pattern: }`.
linechartdata.below_line_bgcolor: Fills the area between the line and the bottom of the chart with this color, for an area chart. Use `"#2563eb,0.2"` for a see-through fill.
linechartdata.below_line_cutoff_y: Stops the area below the line at this y value.
linechartdata.below_line_gradient: Fills the area below the line with a gradient instead, for example from the line color to transparent.
linechartdata.curve_smoothness: How round a `curved` line is, from 0 (straight) to 1 (default 0.35).
linechartdata.curved: Draws a smooth curve through the points instead of straight segments (default false).
linechartdata.dash_pattern: Draws the line dashed: lengths of dashes and gaps in logical pixels, for example `[6, 4]`.
linechartdata.gradient: Gradient along the line instead of `color`.
linechartdata.point: Dot drawn at every point: `true` for the default dot, `false` or unset for none, or a hash with `_type` `"ChartCirclePoint"` (`radius`, `color`, `stroke_color`, `stroke_width`), `"ChartSquarePoint"` (`size`, `color`, `stroke_color`, `stroke_width`) or `"ChartCrossPoint"` (`size`, `width`, `color`).
linechartdata.points: The points of the line, built with [`line_chart_data_point(...)`](/docs/control-line-chart-data-point), in x order.
linechartdata.prevent_curve_over_shooting: Keeps a `curved` line from bulging above or below its points (default false).
linechartdata.prevent_curve_over_shooting_threshold: Smallest gap between two points, in y units, at which `prevent_curve_over_shooting` applies (default 10).
linechartdata.rounded_stroke_cap: Rounds the two ends of the line (default false).
linechartdata.rounded_stroke_join: Rounds the corners where segments meet (default false).
linechartdata.shadow: Shadow drawn under the line, for example `{ color: "#000000,0.2", blur_radius: 4, offset: { x: 0, y: 2 } }`.
linechartdata.step_direction: Draws a step line instead: `0` steps at the start of each segment, `1` at the end and `0.5` in the middle.
linechartdata.stroke_width: Thickness of the line, in logical pixels (default 2).

linechartdatapoint.selected: With `interactive: false` on the chart, highlights the point and shows its bubble permanently (default false).
linechartdatapoint.show_tooltip: Set false to show no bubble for this point (default true).
linechartdatapoint.x: Position of the point on the x axis.
linechartdatapoint.y: Value of the point on the y axis.

listtile.dense: Uses a more compact layout with less vertical space. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.hover_color: Color of the tile while the pointer is over it. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.is_three_line: Gives the subtitle room for two lines, so the tile is three lines tall. iOS and macOS ignore it.
listtile.shape: Shape of the tile's background and tap highlight. iOS and macOS ignore it.

lottie.alignment: Where the animation sits in its box (default centered).
lottie.animate: Plays the animation (default true); set false to stop it on the frame it shows.
lottie.background_loading: Parses the animation off the main thread, for large files.
lottie.enable_layers_opacity: Applies layer opacity to whole layers, which some animations need (default false).
lottie.enable_merge_paths: Turns on Lottie's merge-path support, which some animations need (default false).
lottie.error_content: Control shown instead of the animation when it cannot be loaded; unset, an error box is shown.
lottie.filter_quality: Scaling quality when the content is resized: `"none"`, `"low"`, `"medium"` or `"high"`.
lottie.fit: How the content is sized into its box: `"contain"` (the default), `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"fitWidth"`, `"fitHeight"`, `"none"` or `"scaleDown"`. Write enum values in Flutter's spelling, such as `"fitWidth"`: 0.0.23 does not read `"fit_width"`.
lottie.headers: HTTP headers sent when `src` is a URL, for example `{ "Authorization" => "Bearer ..." }`.
lottie.on_error: Fired when the animation cannot be loaded, and for warnings while parsing it; `event.data` is the message.
lottie.on_load: Fired when the animation has loaded. No data.
lottie.repeat: Plays the animation in a loop (default true).
lottie.reverse: When repeating, plays the animation forward and then backward (default false).
lottie.src: The animation: a URL, a path in your app's assets, a file path on the device, or the JSON as base64 text. Required: without it the control draws an error box.

map.animation_curve: Default easing of the move and zoom methods (default `"fastOutSlowIn"`).
map.animation_duration: Default length of the move and zoom methods, in milliseconds (default 500).
map.bgcolor: Color shown where no tile has loaded yet (default light grey, `"#e0e0e0"`).
map.initial_camera_fit: Opens the map so that an area fits: `{ bounds: { corner_1:, corner_2: } }` or `{ coordinates: [...] }`, with `{ latitude:, longitude: }` hashes (arrays are not converted here), plus optional `padding`, `max_zoom`, `min_zoom` and `force_integer_zoom_level`. It wins over `initial_center` and `initial_zoom`.
map.initial_center: Where the map opens, as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }` (default latitude 50.5, longitude 30.51). Moving the map later does not change it: use the methods below.
map.initial_rotation: Rotation the map opens with, in degrees clockwise (default 0).
map.initial_zoom: Zoom level the map opens at (default 13); each level doubles the scale, and 0 shows the whole world.
map.interaction_configuration: Which gestures move the map, as a hash. `flags` is a sum of gesture bits: 1 drag, 2 fling, 4 pinch-move, 8 pinch-zoom, 16 double-tap zoom, 32 double-tap-drag zoom, 64 scroll-wheel zoom, 128 rotate (default 255, all; `0` makes the map static). Always include `pinch_move_threshold` (flutter_map uses 40): without it the map fails to draw. Also takes `scroll_wheel_velocity`, `pinch_zoom_threshold`, `rotation_threshold` and `enable_multi_finger_gesture_race`.
map.keep_alive: Keeps the map and its loaded tiles alive when it scrolls out of a list (default false).
map.layers: What the map draws, bottom to top: a [`tile_layer`](/docs/control-tile-layer) first, then marker, circle, polyline and polygon layers, and an attribution last. Also the first positional argument: `map([...])`.
map.max_zoom: Largest zoom level the user can reach.
map.min_zoom: Smallest zoom level the user can reach.
map.on_event: Fired for every camera event of the map. `event.data` has `source`, what caused it (such as `"dragStart"`, `"onDrag"`, `"scrollWheel"` or `"mapController"` for your method calls), and `camera`, as in `on_position_change`.
map.on_hover: Fired as a mouse moves over the map, on desktop and web. `event.data["coordinates"]` is the map position; the rest is the pointer: `k` (kind, such as `"touch"` or `"mouse"`), `l` and `g` (local and global `{ "x", "y" }`), `ts`, `dev` and the pressure and size readings.
map.on_init: Fired once, when the map is ready to receive the move and zoom methods. No data.
map.on_long_press: Fired when the user presses the map for a while. `event.data["coordinates"]` is the map position as `{ "latitude" =>, "longitude" => }`; `gx` / `gy` and `lx` / `ly` are the global and map-relative positions in logical pixels.
map.on_pointer_cancel: Fired when the system cancels a pointer, for example when a gesture is taken over. `event.data["coordinates"]` is the map position; the rest is the pointer: `k` (kind, such as `"touch"` or `"mouse"`), `l` and `g` (local and global `{ "x", "y" }`), `ts`, `dev` and the pressure and size readings.
map.on_pointer_down: Fired when a finger or button goes down on the map. `event.data["coordinates"]` is the map position; the rest is the pointer: `k` (kind, such as `"touch"` or `"mouse"`), `l` and `g` (local and global `{ "x", "y" }`), `ts`, `dev` and the pressure and size readings.
map.on_pointer_up: Fired when a finger or button is released. `event.data["coordinates"]` is the map position; the rest is the pointer: `k` (kind, such as `"touch"` or `"mouse"`), `l` and `g` (local and global `{ "x", "y" }`), `ts`, `dev` and the pressure and size readings.
map.on_position_change: Fired as the camera moves, often many times a second. `event.data` has `coordinates` (the new center), `has_gesture` (true when the user moved it) and `camera`: `center`, `zoom`, `min_zoom`, `max_zoom` and `rotation`.
map.on_secondary_tap: Fired on a right click or secondary tap. `event.data["coordinates"]` is the map position as `{ "latitude" =>, "longitude" => }`; `gx` / `gy` and `lx` / `ly` are the global and map-relative positions in logical pixels.
map.on_tap: Fired when the user taps the map. `event.data["coordinates"]` is the map position as `{ "latitude" =>, "longitude" => }`; `gx` / `gy` and `lx` / `ly` are the global and map-relative positions in logical pixels.

marker.alignment: Where the box sits relative to the point, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1: `{ x: 0, y: -1 }` puts it above the point, like a pin (default centered).
marker.content: Control drawn at the point, such as an `icon(...)`. Required; also the first positional argument: `marker(icon("place"), coordinates: ...)`.
marker.coordinates: The point the marker is pinned to, as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`. Required.
marker.height: Height of the marker's box, in logical pixels (default 30).
marker.rotate: Keeps this marker upright when the map rotates; unset, the layer's `rotate` applies.
marker.width: Width of the marker's box, in logical pixels (default 30). The content is laid out in it.

markerlayer.alignment: Where each marker sits relative to its point, unless the marker sets its own (default centered on the point).
markerlayer.markers: The [`marker`](/docs/control-marker) controls to draw. Also the first positional argument: `marker_layer([...])`.
markerlayer.rotate: Keeps the markers upright when the map rotates (default false). A marker's own `rotate` wins.

materialpicker.enable_label: Shows the name and hex code of the selected shade (default false).
materialpicker.on_color_change: Fired as the user picks a color. `event.data` is the new color as `"#aarrggbb"` (alpha first, for example `"#ff2563eb"`), which every color property accepts.
materialpicker.on_primary_change: Fired when the user picks a palette, before choosing a shade; `event.data` is that palette's main color as `"#aarrggbb"`.
materialpicker.portrait_only: Always uses the portrait layout, with the shades under the palette, even when the screen is wide (default false).

multiplechoiceblockpicker.available_colors: The swatches to choose from, as a list of colors. Unset, the picker shows its default palette of Material colors.
multiplechoiceblockpicker.colors: The selected colors, as a list.
multiplechoiceblockpicker.on_colors_change: Fired when the user selects or deselects a swatch; `event.data` is the list of selected colors as `"#aarrggbb"` strings.

nativead.factory_id: Id of a native ad factory registered in the Flutter client. You need `factory_id` or `template_style`.
nativead.on_click: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.on_close: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.on_error: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.on_impression: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.on_load: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.on_open: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.on_paid: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.on_will_dismiss: Not sent yet: the client does not draw native ads.
nativead.request: Targeting of the ad request, as on `banner_ad`.
nativead.template_style: Google's ready-made layout: `{ template_type: "small" or "medium", main_bgcolor:, corner_radius:, primary_text_style:, secondary_text_style:, tertiary_text_style:, call_to_action_text_style: }`.
nativead.unit_id: Your AdMob native ad unit id. Unset, Google's test native unit is used.

navigationrail.group_alignment: Vertical position of the destinations, from -1.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom).

oval.height: Height of the ellipse, in logical pixels (default 0).
oval.paint: How the shape is drawn, built with `paint(...)`: `color` (default black), `style` (`"fill"`, the default, or `"stroke"`), `stroke_width`, `stroke_cap` (`"butt"`, `"round"`, `"square"`), `stroke_join` (`"miter"`, `"round"`, `"bevel"`), `stroke_dash_pattern` (dash and gap lengths, for example `[8, 4]`), `blend_mode`, `anti_alias` (default true), `blur_image` and `gradient`.
oval.width: Width of the ellipse, in logical pixels (default 0).
oval.x: Left edge of the box that holds the ellipse. Required.
oval.y: Top edge of the box that holds the ellipse. Required.

path.elements: The drawing steps, in order: `path_move_to(x, y)`, `path_line_to(x, y)`, `path_quadratic_to(cp1x:, cp1y:, x:, y:, w: 1)` (it draws a straight line unless you pass `w: 1`), `path_cubic_to(cp1x:, cp1y:, cp2x:, cp2y:, x:, y:)`, `path_arc(x:, y:, width:, height:, start_angle:, sweep_angle:)`, `path_arc_to(x:, y:, radius:, rotation:, large_arc:, clockwise:)`, `path_oval(x:, y:, width:, height:)`, `path_rect(x:, y:, width:, height:, border_radius:)`, `path_sub_path(elements:, x:, y:)` and `path_close`.
path.paint: How the shape is drawn, built with `paint(...)`: `color` (default black), `style` (`"fill"`, the default, or `"stroke"`), `stroke_width`, `stroke_cap` (`"butt"`, `"round"`, `"square"`), `stroke_join` (`"miter"`, `"round"`, `"bevel"`), `stroke_dash_pattern` (dash and gap lengths, for example `[8, 4]`), `blend_mode`, `anti_alias` (default true), `blur_image` and `gradient`.

piechart.animation: How the chart animates when its data changes: a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration:, curve: }` (default 150 ms, `"linear"`).
piechart.center_space_color: Color of the hole in the middle.
piechart.center_space_radius: Radius of the hole in the middle, in logical pixels. Unset, the hole takes all the room the slices leave; `0` draws a full pie.
piechart.height: Height in logical pixels. In a parent with unbounded height, such as a `column` in a scrolling page, the chart is at most 300 pixels tall; set `height` to change it.
piechart.on_event: Fired as the user touches or hovers the pie, always: this chart has no `interactive` switch. `event.data` has `type`, `section_index` (`nil` outside the slices) and `local_x` / `local_y`, the touch position in the chart. `event.data["type"]` is the touch phase: `"tapDown"`, `"tapUp"`, `"tapCancel"`, `"panStart"`, `"panUpdate"`, `"panEnd"`, `"longPressStart"`, `"longPressMoveUpdate"`, `"longPressEnd"`, or on desktop and web `"pointerEnter"`, `"pointerHover"` and `"pointerExit"`. The chart sends an event only when this data changes.
piechart.sections: The slices, built with [`pie_chart_section(...)`](/docs/control-pie-chart-section), drawn clockwise.
piechart.sections_space: Gap between two slices, in logical pixels (default 2).
piechart.start_degree_offset: Angle, in degrees, where the first slice starts; 0 (the default) is the 3 o'clock position.

piechartsection.badge: Control drawn on the slice, such as an `icon(...)`. Unlike other controls, `badge` is not a corner badge here.
piechartsection.badge_position: Where the badge sits along the slice, from 0 (inner edge) to 1 (outer edge) (default 0.5).
piechartsection.border_side: Outline of the slice, for example `{ color: "#ffffff", width: 2 }`.
piechartsection.color: Fill color of the slice (default cyan).
piechartsection.gradient: Gradient that fills the slice instead of `color`.
piechartsection.radius: Length of the slice from the hole to the outer edge, in logical pixels (default 40).
piechartsection.title: Text drawn on the slice. No text is drawn when unset.
piechartsection.title_position: Where the title sits along the slice, from 0 (inner edge) to 1 (outer edge) (default 0.5).
piechartsection.title_style: Style of the title, for example `{ size: 12, color: "#ffffff", weight: "bold" }`.
piechartsection.value: Size of the slice; slices share the circle in proportion to their values (default 10).

points.paint: How the points are drawn, built with `paint(...)`: `color` (default black), `style` (`"fill"`, the default, or `"stroke"`), `stroke_width`, `stroke_cap` (`"butt"`, `"round"`, `"square"`), `stroke_join` (`"miter"`, `"round"`, `"bevel"`), `stroke_dash_pattern` (dash and gap lengths, for example `[8, 4]`), `blend_mode`, `anti_alias` (default true), `blur_image` and `gradient`. `stroke_width` is the dot size, and `stroke_cap: "round"` makes round dots.
points.point_mode: `"points"` (the default) draws a dot per point, `"lines"` joins them in pairs, and `"polygon"` joins them all in order.
points.points: The points, each `[x, y]` or `{ x:, y: }`.

polygonlayer.draw_labels_last: Draws all labels after all polygons, so no polygon covers a label (default false).
polygonlayer.polygon_culling: Skips polygons outside the screen (default true).
polygonlayer.polygons: The [`polygon_marker`](/docs/control-polygon-marker) controls to draw. Also the first positional argument: `polygon_layer([...])`.
polygonlayer.simplification_tolerance: How much outlines are simplified at lower zoom levels to draw faster; `0` keeps every point (default 0.3).
polygonlayer.use_alternative_rendering: Uses a different drawing method that can be faster for many simple polygons (default false). Measure before enabling it.

polygonmarker.border_stroke_width: Outline thickness, in logical pixels (default 0, no outline).
polygonmarker.color: Fill color (default `"#4caf50"`); use `"#7c3aed,0.25"` to keep the map visible under it.
polygonmarker.coordinates: The corners of the area, in order, each as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`.
polygonmarker.disable_holes_border: Draws no outline around holes in the area (default false).
polygonmarker.label: Text drawn in the middle of the area.
polygonmarker.label_text_style: Style of the label, for example `{ size: 12, weight: "bold" }`.
polygonmarker.rotate_label: Turns the label with the map instead of keeping it level (default false).
polygonmarker.stroke_cap: Shape of the outline ends: `"round"` (the default), `"butt"` or `"square"`.
polygonmarker.stroke_join: Shape of the outline corners: `"round"` (the default), `"miter"` or `"bevel"`.

polylinelayer.culling_margin: How far beyond the screen, in logical pixels, line segments are still drawn (default 10).
polylinelayer.min_hittable_radius: Smallest touch area around each line, in logical pixels (default 10).
polylinelayer.polylines: The [`polyline_marker`](/docs/control-polyline-marker) controls to draw. Also the first positional argument: `polyline_layer([...])`.
polylinelayer.simplification_tolerance: How much lines are simplified at lower zoom levels to draw faster; `0` keeps every point (default 0.3).

polylinemarker.border_color: Color of the outline drawn on both sides of the line (default `"#ffeb3b"`).
polylinemarker.border_stroke_width: Thickness of that outline, in logical pixels (default 0, no outline).
polylinemarker.colors_stop: Where each of `gradient_colors` sits along the line, from 0 to 1.
polylinemarker.coordinates: The points of the line, in order, each as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`.
polylinemarker.gradient_colors: Colors blended along the line instead of `color`, for example from green to red.
polylinemarker.stroke_cap: Shape of the line ends: `"round"` (the default), `"butt"` or `"square"`.
polylinemarker.stroke_join: Shape of the corners: `"round"` (the default), `"miter"` or `"bevel"`.
polylinemarker.stroke_pattern: `{ _type: "solid" }` (the default), `{ _type: "dotted", spacing_factor: 1.5 }` or `{ _type: "dashed", segments: [10, 5] }`; dotted and dashed also take `pattern_fit` (default `"scaleUp"`).
polylinemarker.stroke_width: Line thickness, in logical pixels, or in meters with `use_stroke_width_in_meter` (default 1).
polylinemarker.use_stroke_width_in_meter: Measures `stroke_width` in meters on the ground (default false).

popupmenubutton.on_select: Fired when an item is chosen; the data is the item's internal id, so handle each item's `on_click` instead.

progressring.animating: On iOS and macOS, spins the indeterminate indicator while true; set `false` to pause it. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.radius: Radius of the activity indicator on iOS and macOS, in logical pixels. Android, web, Windows and Linux ignore it.
progressring.stroke_cap: Shape of the ring's line ends: `"butt"`, `"round"` or `"square"`. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.track_gap: Gap between the active and inactive parts of the ring's track, in logical pixels. iOS and macOS ignore it.
progressring.year_2023: On Android, web, Windows and Linux, uses the 2023 Material 3 design; set `false` for the newer look.

radarchart.animation: How the chart animates when its data changes: a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration:, curve: }` (default 150 ms, `"linear"`).
radarchart.border: Border drawn around the plot area, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`. No border is drawn when unset.
radarchart.center_min_value: Puts the smallest value at the center instead of the first ring (default false).
radarchart.data_sets: The shapes drawn on the radar, built with [`radar_data_set(...)`](/docs/control-radar-data-set). Every data set needs the same number of entries.
radarchart.grid_border_side: Lines of the spokes (default 2 pixels wide).
radarchart.height: Height in logical pixels. In a parent with unbounded height, such as a `column` in a scrolling page, the chart is at most 300 pixels tall; set `height` to change it.
radarchart.interactive: When false, or when the chart is `disabled`, touches are ignored (default true).
radarchart.long_press_duration: How long a press must last, in milliseconds, before it counts as a long press for `on_event`.
radarchart.on_event: Fired as the user touches or hovers the chart. `event.data` has `type`, `data_set_index`, `entry_index` and `entry_value`; they are `nil` when no entry is touched. `event.data["type"]` is the touch phase: `"tapDown"`, `"tapUp"`, `"tapCancel"`, `"panStart"`, `"panUpdate"`, `"panEnd"`, `"longPressStart"`, `"longPressMoveUpdate"`, `"longPressEnd"`, or on desktop and web `"pointerEnter"`, `"pointerHover"` and `"pointerExit"`. The chart sends an event only when this data changes.
radarchart.radar_border_side: Outline of the radar, for example `{ color: "#9ca3af", width: 1 }` (default 2 pixels wide).
radarchart.radar_shape: Shape of the grid: `"polygon"` (the default) or `"circle"`.
radarchart.tick_border_side: Lines of the rings (default 2 pixels wide).
radarchart.tick_count: Number of rings between the center and the edge (default 1).
radarchart.ticks_text_style: Style of the value labels on the rings.
radarchart.title_position_percentage_offset: How far the titles sit from the edge, as a fraction of the radius (default 0.2).
radarchart.titles: Labels of the spokes, built with [`radar_chart_title(...)`](/docs/control-radar-chart-title), one per entry and in the same order.
radarchart.touch_spot_threshold: How close a touch must be to an entry, in logical pixels, to count as touching it.

radarcharttitle.angle: Rotation of the label, in degrees. Unset, the label turns with its spoke.
radarcharttitle.position_percentage_offset: How far this label sits from the edge, as a fraction of the radius; overrides the chart's `title_position_percentage_offset`.
radarcharttitle.text_spans: Extra styled text after `text`, built with `text_span(...)`.

radardataset.border_width: Thickness of the outline, in logical pixels (default 2).
radardataset.entries: Values of the shape, built with [`radar_data_set_entry(...)`](/docs/control-radar-data-set-entry), one per spoke in spoke order.
radardataset.entry_radius: Radius of the dot drawn at each entry, in logical pixels (default 5).
radardataset.fill_color: Color inside the shape (default `"#00bcd4"`); use `"#2563eb,0.25"` to see the other data sets through it.
radardataset.fill_gradient: Gradient inside the shape instead of `fill_color`.

rect.border_radius: Rounds the corners: a number, or `{ top_left:, top_right:, bottom_left:, bottom_right: }`.
rect.paint: How the shape is drawn, built with `paint(...)`: `color` (default black), `style` (`"fill"`, the default, or `"stroke"`), `stroke_width`, `stroke_cap` (`"butt"`, `"round"`, `"square"`), `stroke_join` (`"miter"`, `"round"`, `"bevel"`), `stroke_dash_pattern` (dash and gap lengths, for example `[8, 4]`), `blend_mode`, `anti_alias` (default true), `blur_image` and `gradient`.
rect.x: Left edge of the rectangle. Required.
rect.y: Top edge of the rectangle. Required.

reorderablelistview.spacing: Space between items, in logical pixels.

responsiverow.columns: Number of virtual columns the row is divided into (default 12); `col` spans count in these.

richattribution.alignment: Corner the button and popup sit in: `"bottomRight"` (the default) or `"bottomLeft"`.
richattribution.attributions: What the attribution lists: [`text_source_attribution`](/docs/control-text-source-attribution) and [`image_source_attribution`](/docs/control-image-source-attribution) controls. Also the first positional argument.
richattribution.permanent_height: Height of the logos that always stay visible, in logical pixels (default 24).
richattribution.popup_bgcolor: Background of the popup that lists the text attributions.
richattribution.popup_initial_display_duration: How long, in milliseconds, the popup stays open after the map opens (default 0, closed).
richattribution.show_flutter_map_attribution: Adds the flutter_map logo and a "Made with flutter_map" line (default true).

rive.alignment: Where the artboard sits in its box (default centered).
rive.animations: Names of the animations to play, for example `["idle"]`.
rive.art_board: Name of the artboard to show (default the file's default artboard).
rive.clip_rect: Shows only this part of the artboard: `{ left:, top:, right:, bottom: }` in artboard pixels.
rive.fit: How the content is sized into its box: `"contain"` (the default), `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"fitWidth"`, `"fitHeight"`, `"none"` or `"scaleDown"`. Write enum values in Flutter's spelling, such as `"fitWidth"`: 0.0.23 does not read `"fit_width"`.
rive.headers: HTTP headers sent when `src` is a URL.
rive.placeholder: Control shown while the file loads, such as `progress_ring()`.
rive.src: The `.riv` file: a URL, a path in your app's assets or a file path on the device. Required: without it the control draws an error box.
rive.state_machines: Names of the state machines to run; they receive the user's touches. With neither `animations` nor `state_machines`, the artboard's default state machine runs, or else its first animation.
rive.use_art_board_size: Sizes the control to the artboard instead of the space it gets (default false).

scatterchart.animation: How the chart animates when its data changes: a duration in milliseconds, or `{ duration:, curve: }` (default 150 ms, `"linear"`).
scatterchart.baseline_x: x value the top and bottom axis labels are counted from (default 0).
scatterchart.baseline_y: y value the left and right axis labels are counted from (default 0).
scatterchart.border: Border drawn around the plot area, for example `{ color: "#d1d5db", width: 1 }`. No border is drawn when unset.
scatterchart.bottom_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
scatterchart.error_indicator_data: Accepted but not drawn by the client: error bars are not supported yet.
scatterchart.height: Height in logical pixels. In a parent with unbounded height, such as a `column` in a scrolling page, the chart is at most 300 pixels tall; set `height` to change it.
scatterchart.horizontal_grid_lines: Horizontal grid lines as a hash: `interval` (in y units), `color`, `width` (default 2), `dash_pattern` (for example `[4, 4]`) and `gradient`. Pass `{}` for the default lines. No grid is drawn when both grid properties are unset.
scatterchart.interactive: When false, or when the chart is `disabled`, touches are ignored and `on_event` is not sent (default true).
scatterchart.left_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
scatterchart.long_press_duration: How long a press must last, in milliseconds, before it counts as a long press for `on_event`.
scatterchart.max_x: Largest value on the x axis. Unset, the chart fits the spots.
scatterchart.max_y: Largest value on the y axis. Unset, the chart fits the spots.
scatterchart.min_x: Smallest value on the x axis. Unset, the chart fits the spots.
scatterchart.min_y: Smallest value on the y axis. Unset, the chart fits the spots.
scatterchart.on_event: Fired as the user touches or hovers the chart. `event.data` has `type` and `spot_index`, the index of the touched spot or `nil`. `event.data["type"]` is the touch phase: `"tapDown"`, `"tapUp"`, `"tapCancel"`, `"panStart"`, `"panUpdate"`, `"panEnd"`, `"longPressStart"`, `"longPressMoveUpdate"`, `"longPressEnd"`, or on desktop and web `"pointerEnter"`, `"pointerHover"` and `"pointerExit"`. The chart sends an event only when this data changes.
scatterchart.right_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
scatterchart.rotation_quarter_turns: Rotates the whole chart by quarter turns clockwise: `1` draws it sideways (default `0`).
scatterchart.show_tooltips_for_selected_spots_only: When true, the chart stops showing bubbles under the finger and shows them only for spots marked `selected: true` (default false).
scatterchart.tooltip: Style of the touch bubble, as on the other charts. Scatter charts show no bubble yet, because Ruflet cannot set its text, so use `on_event` to show the touched spot.
scatterchart.top_axis: Axis on this side, built with [`chart_axis(...)`](/docs/control-chart-axis). Without one the side shows no labels.
scatterchart.vertical_grid_lines: Vertical grid lines as a hash: `interval` (in x units), `color`, `width` (default 2), `dash_pattern` and `gradient`. Pass `{}` for the default lines.

scatterchartspot.color: Color of the dot. Unset, the chart picks one of 18 series colors from the spot's position.
scatterchartspot.label_text: Text drawn next to the dot.
scatterchartspot.label_text_style: Style of `label_text`; unset, the text takes the dot's color.
scatterchartspot.point: Custom dot instead of `radius` and `color`: a hash with `_type` `"ChartCirclePoint"`, `"ChartSquarePoint"` or `"ChartCrossPoint"`, as on [`line_chart_data`](/docs/control-line-chart-data).
scatterchartspot.radius: Radius of the dot, in logical pixels.
scatterchartspot.render_priority: Drawing order: spots with a higher number are drawn on top (default 0).
scatterchartspot.selected: Marks the spot for a permanent bubble (default false); scatter charts show no bubble yet, so it has no visible effect.
scatterchartspot.show_tooltip: Set false to show no bubble for this spot (default true).
scatterchartspot.x_error: Not supported yet: leave it unset, as a value stops the chart from drawing.
scatterchartspot.y_error: Not supported yet: leave it unset, as a value stops the chart from drawing.

searchbar.shrink_wrap: Sizes the search view to its suggestions.

semantics.header: Marks the content as a heading for screen readers.
semantics.expanded: Tells screen readers whether the content is expanded.
semantics.on_tap_hint_text: What screen readers say the tap action does, for example "Open".
semantics.on_long_press_hint_text: What screen readers say the long-press action does.
semantics.hint_text: What screen readers say acting on the control does, for example "Opens the message".
semantics.focus: Tells screen readers whether the control has input focus.
semantics.textfield: Tells screen readers that the content is a text field.
semantics.identifier: An identifier for UI tests and platform accessibility tools; screen readers do not announce it.

shadow.elevation: How high the outline floats above the canvas; higher values give a larger, softer shadow (default 0).
shadow.path: Outline that casts the shadow, as a list of path elements like those of [`path`](/docs/control-path), for example `[path_rect(x: 20, y: 20, width: 120, height: 70)]`.
shadow.transparent_occluder: Set true when the shape over the shadow is see-through, so the shadow is also drawn under it (default false).

simpleattribution.alignment: Corner of the map the badge sits in, as `{ x:, y: }` from -1 to 1 (default bottom right).
simpleattribution.bgcolor: Background of the badge (default the theme's surface color).
simpleattribution.on_click: Fired when the badge is tapped, for example to open the provider's copyright page. No data.
simpleattribution.text: Attribution text, as a string. On iOS and macOS it follows "flutter_map |" and a copyright sign.

slidepicker.color_model: Which sliders to show: `"rgb"` (the default), `"hsv"` or `"hsl"`.
slidepicker.display_thumb_color: Fills the slider thumbs with the selected color (default true).
slidepicker.indicator_alignment_begin: Start of the bar's checkerboard and color gradient, as `{ x:, y: }` (default `{ x: -1, y: -3 }`).
slidepicker.indicator_alignment_end: End of that gradient, as `{ x:, y: }` (default `{ x: 1, y: 3 }`).
slidepicker.indicator_size: Size of that bar, as `{ width:, height: }` (default 280 by 50).
slidepicker.label_types: Value fields shown under the sliders: any of `"hex"`, `"rgb"`, `"hsv"` and `"hsl"` (default none).
slidepicker.on_color_change: Fired as the user picks a color. `event.data` is the new color as `"#aarrggbb"` (alpha first, for example `"#ff2563eb"`), which every color property accepts.
slidepicker.show_indicator: Shows a bar filled with the selected color (default true).
slidepicker.show_label: Shows the value fields listed in `label_types` (default true).
slidepicker.show_params: Shows each slider's name and value (default true).
slidepicker.show_slider_text: Shows the value as text next to each slider (default true).
slidepicker.slider_size: Size of each slider, as `{ width:, height: }` (default 260 by 40).

snackbar.action: Label of the action button shown in the snack bar.
snackbar.duration: How long the snack bar stays visible, in milliseconds.

spinkit.variant: The indicator style; set it with the variant keyword you pass to `spinkit`, such as `three_bounce:`.
spinkit.size: Size of the indicator, in logical pixels (default 50).
spinkit.duration: Length of one animation cycle, in milliseconds.

textsourceattribution.on_click: Fired when the text is tapped. No data.
textsourceattribution.prepend_copyright: Puts a copyright sign before the text (default true).
textsourceattribution.text: Name of the data source, as a string. Also the first positional argument.
textsourceattribution.text_style: Style of the text, for example `{ size: 12 }`.

tilelayer.additional_options: Values for your own placeholders in `url_template`, for example `{ "access_token" => "..." }` for `{access_token}`.
tilelayer.display_mode: How new tiles appear: `{ _type: "fadein", duration: 100, start_opacity:, reload_start_opacity: }` (the default fades in over 100 ms) or `{ _type: "instantaneous", opacity: 1.0 }`.
tilelayer.enable_retina_mode: Draws sharper tiles on high-density screens: with a `{r}` placeholder in `url_template` the server's retina tiles, otherwise four tiles per tile (default false).
tilelayer.enable_tms: Numbers tile rows from the bottom, for TMS servers (default false).
tilelayer.error_image_src: Image shown in place of a tile that failed to load: a URL or asset path.
tilelayer.evict_error_tile_strategy: What happens to tiles that failed to load: `"none"` (the default), `"dispose"`, `"notVisible"` or `"notVisibleRespectMargin"`.
tilelayer.fallback_url: Second address template, tried when a tile fails to load from `url_template`.
tilelayer.keep_buffer: How many rows and columns of tiles to keep beyond the screen after moving (default 2).
tilelayer.max_native_zoom: Largest zoom the server has tiles for; above it the layer scales up those tiles (default 19).
tilelayer.max_zoom: Largest map zoom at which this layer shows tiles (no limit by default).
tilelayer.min_native_zoom: Smallest zoom the server has tiles for; below it the layer scales up those tiles (default 0).
tilelayer.min_zoom: Smallest map zoom at which this layer shows tiles (default 0).
tilelayer.on_image_error: Fired when a tile fails to load; `event.data` is the error message.
tilelayer.pan_buffer: How many rows and columns of tiles to load beyond the screen ahead of time (default 1).
tilelayer.tile_bounds: Loads tiles only inside this area: `{ corner_1:, corner_2: }` with `{ latitude:, longitude: }` hashes (arrays are not converted here).
tilelayer.tile_size: Size of one tile, in logical pixels (default 256).
tilelayer.url_template: Address of the tiles, with `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}` placeholders, `{s}` for a subdomain and your own `{name}` placeholders from `additional_options`. Check the provider's usage policy.
tilelayer.user_agent_package_name: Your app identifier, sent in the `User-Agent` of tile requests on native platforms (default `"unknown"`). OpenStreetMap asks apps to set it.
tilelayer.zoom_offset: Number added to the zoom level of every tile request (default 0).
tilelayer.zoom_reverse: Counts zoom levels down instead of up in tile requests, for servers that number them that way (default false).

video.alignment: Where the video sits in its box when it does not fill it (default centered).
video.autoplay: Starts playing as soon as the player is created (default false).
video.configuration: Player settings, read when the player is created: `output_driver`, `hardware_decoding_api`, `enable_hardware_acceleration` (default true), `width`, `height`, `scale` and, on desktop and mobile, `mpv_properties` passed to the mpv player.
video.fill_color: Color of the bars around a video that does not fill its box (default black).
video.filter_quality: Scaling quality when the content is resized: `"none"`, `"low"`, `"medium"` or `"high"` (default `"low"`).
video.fit: How the content is sized into its box: `"contain"` (the default), `"cover"`, `"fill"`, `"fitWidth"`, `"fitHeight"`, `"none"` or `"scaleDown"`. Write enum values in Flutter's spelling, such as `"fitWidth"`: 0.0.23 does not read `"fit_width"`.
video.fullscreen: Set true to show the video fullscreen and false to leave; the client also sets it when the user uses the fullscreen button.
video.muted: Starts the player muted (default false). It is read when the player is created.
video.on_complete: Fired when a clip finishes or starts again; `event.data` is `true` when it has completed.
video.on_enter_fullscreen: Fired when the video goes fullscreen. No data.
video.on_error: Fired when a clip cannot be played; `event.data` is the error message.
video.on_exit_fullscreen: Fired when the video leaves fullscreen. No data.
video.on_loaded: Fired when the player is ready. No data.
video.on_track_change: Fired when the playlist moves to another clip; `event.data` is its index, starting at 0.
video.pause_upon_entering_background_mode: Pauses when the app goes to the background (default true).
video.pitch: Pitch of the sound, where 1.0 is normal; set it when the player is created to allow changing it later.
video.playlist: What to play: a list of hashes, or one hash, with `resource` (a URL or a file path on the device, passed to the player as is) and optional `http_headers` and `extras`. It is read when the player is created; change it later with `playlist_add`, `playlist_remove` and `jump_to`.
video.playlist_mode: What happens at the end of a clip: `"none"` stops at the end of the playlist, `"single"` repeats the current clip and `"loop"` repeats the whole playlist.
video.resume_upon_entering_foreground_mode: Resumes when the app comes back to the foreground (default false).
video.show_controls: Draws the play, seek and fullscreen controls over the video (default true): Cupertino-style on iOS and macOS, Material elsewhere.
video.shuffle_playlist: Plays the playlist in random order.
video.subtitle_configuration: How subtitles look: `{ text_style:, visible:, text_scale_factor:, text_align:, padding: }` (default white 32-pixel text on a dark band).
video.subtitle_track: Subtitles to show: `{ src: "auto" }`, `{ src: "none" }`, or `{ src:, title:, language: }` where `src` is a URL, a file path or the subtitle text itself.
video.title: Name of the player shown by the operating system, for example in desktop media controls (default `"ruflet-video"`).
video.wakelock: Keeps the screen on while the video plays (default true).

WebView.can_go_back: The block receives `(true or false, error)`: whether there is a page to go back to.
WebView.can_go_forward: The block receives `(true or false, error)`: whether there is a page to go forward to.
WebView.enable_zoom: Lets the user pinch to zoom.
WebView.go_back: Goes back one page, when there is one.
WebView.go_forward: Goes forward one page, when there is one.
WebView.load_file: Loads an HTML file from an absolute path on the device.
WebView.load_html: Shows an HTML string; `base_url:` sets the address that relative links resolve against.
WebView.load_request: Loads a URL with `method:` `"get"` (the default) or `"post"`.
WebView.run_javascript: Runs JavaScript in the page, for example to hide a node. It returns no result.
WebView.scroll_to: Scrolls the page to the `x`, `y` position, in pixels.
WebView.set_javascript_mode: `"unrestricted"` turns JavaScript on and `"disabled"` turns it off. Until you call it, the platform decides: off on Android, on in iOS and macOS.

audio.get_current_position: `on_result` receives the position as a String of microseconds (for example `"184000000"` for 3 min 4 s), or `nil` before the media is loaded.
audio.get_duration: `on_result` receives the length as a String of microseconds (for example `"184000000"` for 3 min 4 s), or `nil` before the media is loaded.
audio.play: Plays from `position:` in milliseconds, which defaults to 0: `play` always starts at the beginning. Use `resume` to continue after `pause`.
audio.release: Frees the player's resources; the next `play` or `resume` loads `src` again.
audio.seek: Jumps to a position in milliseconds; `on_seek_complete` follows.

canvas.capture: Paints the current shapes into a picture that the canvas keeps and draws under its shapes from then on, so you can empty `shapes` without losing the drawing. `pixel_ratio:` sets its resolution (default the screen's). It does nothing before the canvas is painted or when it has no shapes.
canvas.clear_capture: Drops the captured picture, so only the current shapes are drawn.
canvas.get_capture: `on_result` receives the last capture as PNG bytes (a binary String), or `nil` before the first `capture`.

contextmenu.open: On iOS and macOS the menu cannot be opened from code; it opens only from the user's long press.

interstitialad.show: Shows the loaded ad over the whole screen. Call it after `on_load`: before that, it does nothing.

map.center_on: Animates the camera so the point (`[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`) is in the middle, at `zoom:` when given. Options: `animation_curve:` and `animation_duration:` (milliseconds), which default to the map's own, `cancel_ongoing_animations:`, `timeout:` and `on_result:`.
map.move_to: Animates the camera to `destination:` (a point as `[latitude, longitude]` or `{ latitude:, longitude: }`), and to `zoom:` and `rotation:` (degrees) when given; `offset:` shifts the result by `{ x:, y: }` pixels. Options: `animation_curve:` and `animation_duration:` (milliseconds), which default to the map's own, `cancel_ongoing_animations:`, `timeout:` and `on_result:`.
map.reset_rotation: Turns the map back so north is up. Options: `animation_curve:` and `animation_duration:` (milliseconds), which default to the map's own, `cancel_ongoing_animations:`, `timeout:` and `on_result:`.
map.rotate_from: Turns the map by the given number of degrees from its current rotation. Options: `animation_curve:` and `animation_duration:` (milliseconds), which default to the map's own, `cancel_ongoing_animations:`, `timeout:` and `on_result:`.
map.zoom_in: Zooms in by one level. Options: `animation_curve:` and `animation_duration:` (milliseconds), which default to the map's own, `cancel_ongoing_animations:`, `timeout:` and `on_result:`.
map.zoom_out: Zooms out by one level. Options: `animation_curve:` and `animation_duration:` (milliseconds), which default to the map's own, `cancel_ongoing_animations:`, `timeout:` and `on_result:`.
map.zoom_to: Zooms to the given level. Options: `animation_curve:` and `animation_duration:` (milliseconds), which default to the map's own, `cancel_ongoing_animations:`, `timeout:` and `on_result:`.

video.get_current_position: `on_result` receives the position as a String of microseconds (for example `"184000000"` for 3 min 4 s), or `nil` before the media is loaded.
video.get_duration: `on_result` receives the length of the current clip as a String of microseconds (for example `"184000000"` for 3 min 4 s), or `nil` before the media is loaded.
video.is_completed: `on_result` receives `true` when the current clip has finished.
video.jump_to: Moves to the clip at this index, starting at 0.
video.next: Moves to the next clip of the playlist.
video.play_or_pause: Pauses when playing and plays when paused.
video.playlist_add: Adds a clip at the end of the playlist: a hash like those of `playlist`, or keywords, for example `playlist_add(resource: "https://...")`.
video.playlist_remove: Removes the clip at this index.
video.seek: Jumps to a position in milliseconds in the current clip.
video.stop: Stops playback and reloads the playlist without playing it.
